preamble: Reduction of unstressed /e/ to schwa [ə]. In English, late Old English unstressed vowels fell together, and by Early Middle English all unstressed vowels were written <e>, representing /ə/. In Eastern Catalan the reduction is an active stress-conditioned alternation: unstressed /e/ and /ɛ/ are realized as [ə], while Valencian keeps [e].

examples.note: Unstressed vowels merged and were written <e>, representing /ə/, by Early Middle English; final /ə/ was lost around Chaucer's time (Modern 'sun').
In Eastern Catalan the unstressed vowels /a/, /e/ and /ɛ/ reduce to [ə]; Valencian does not reduce /e/.

sources: Wikipedia (2026). Middle English phonology: Unstressed vowels. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_English_phonology
Wiktionary (2026). sun (from Middle English sonne < Old English sunne). https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/sun
allophones_note: Synchronic in Eastern Catalan; historical in English, where the reduction became phonemic
